the LAB‐based mixture (LAB‐M) can be used as a co‐adjuvent with 5‐FU in the treatment of cancer.
the LAB mixture is a potential co‐adjunct for 5‐FU chemotherapy in breast cancer treatment.
the selected mixture of lactic acid bacteria, which is a combination of a vitamin‐producing strain and an immunomutating strain, is a potential co‐adjunct for chemotherapy in breast cancer.

the development of new therapeutic agents for breast cancer, based on the combination of 5‐FU chemotherapy with LAB.
the development of a new therapeutic strategy for cancer treatment based on the combined use of 5‐FU and a LAB mixture, as well as with the identification of the mechanisms of action involved.
the use of selected lactic bacteria as a co‐adjuvants in chemotherapy for cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the LAB mixture is able to enhance 5‐FU‐induced cytotoxicity in vitro and to improve 5‐FU efficacy in a breast cancer mouse model, and that it may be a promising co‐adjuvanat in the treatment of cancer.
the selected LAB strains were able to increase the cytotoxic effects of 5‐FU on breast cancer cell line (4T1) and to improve the efficacy of 5‐fluouracil (FU) in breast cancer mouse model (4T1).

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have demonstrated that LAB are able to modulate the immune response in vitro and in vivo and that they can be used in combination with 5‐FU chemotherapy to reduce tumour burden in a 4T 1 cell mouse model of breast cancer.
the LAB‐based co‐adjuvants are effective and safe for the treatment of cancer.
the combination of 5‐FU with the LAB mixture was effective in inhibiting the growth of the 4T1 cells in vitro and in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a mixture of three lactic acid bacteria strains can be a potential co‐therapeutic for 5‐FU chemotherapy in the treatment of breast cancer.
the use of LAB‐5‐FU combination can be an effective treatment for breast cancer.
